subject: Pilot cost anchors & batching scope — follow-up
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@pinecard.io>, Trevor Shaw <trevor@pinecard.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot cost anchors & batching scope — follow-up

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and the concrete next steps we landed on so things don't get lost. Short version up top, details below.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: token spend unpredictability and peak latency during batch settlement flows.
- Goal: validate a pilot that reduces per-authorization token cost by ~40% while keeping p99 latency < 300ms for the critical path.
- Next immediate actions: we (Redwood) will deliver a TCO workbook + two pilot configs by Friday; PineCard to confirm 90-day pilot budget threshold and a sample traffic window.

Key pain points you shared
- Daily peaks from batch settlement window (14:00–16:00 PT) spike token usage 3–4x. Cost unpredictability is blocking SRE buy-in.
- Some on-prem compliance constraints mean you need a Private option for settlement fingerprints.
- Current latency spikes during micro-bursts cause a measurable increase in failed authorizations when third-party fraud checks run.

What we discussed as levers
1) Batching: move infrequent calls into a controlled batching window for settlement-only flows; expected token savings ~25–35% depending on batch size.
2) KV/prefix caching: cache stable prefixes (merchant metadata) to avoid re-encoding; low latency overhead, adds ~5–10% further savings.
3) Quantized model variant for non-legal text (summaries/labels) — up to 15% CPU/GPU cost reduction with small quality tradeoff.
4) Routing policy: route non-auth real-time flows to hosted tier and keep settlement bursts on Dedicated/Private to control concurrency.

Preliminary pilot scope options (we'll include these in the attached workbook):
- Scope A — Minimal: 30 days, 1 settlement queue, batching at 8–12 requests (low-risk).
- Scope B — Target: 60–90 days, two queues (auth + settlement), KV cache enabled, candidate quantized model for summaries.

Immediate asks from PineCard
- Confirm the 90-day budget ceiling (ballpark number fine) so we can size Dedicated capacity.
- Share a 3-day sample of settlement traffic (anonymous IDs okay) focused on the 14:00–16:00 PT window.
- Any compliance gating items we should surface now for Private deployment (encryption at rest, KMS preference).

Attachments: redwood-tco-draft.xlsx (TCO assumptions and simple model), pinecard-pilot-scope.pdf (two pilot configs).

I'll get the workbook and two proposal configurations over by EOD Friday.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-4343

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@pinecard.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot cost anchors & batching scope — follow-up

Thanks Vanessa — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications and one constraint from procurement: 

Clarifications from our side
- 14:00–16:00 PT is correct; peaks occur closer to 14:30 when multiple issuers close their books.
- Successful authorizations drop by ~2% during the top 30 minutes of the window; even small latency improvements are meaningful for us.
- We can provide an S3 export of anonymized settlement payloads for a 72-hour window — would that be sufficient?

Procurement constraint
- We have an internal pilot cap of $45k for any vendor POC without legal sign-off. If the pilot estimate requires more than that we need a procurement exception or a phased billing plan.

Compliance notes
- KMS preference: AWS KMS with customer key (we can provide ARN).
- No outbound logs with PII to vendor-managed buckets; redacted event samples are fine.

Next steps from PineCard
- I'll confirm the $45k ceiling with finance today and flag any exceptions.
- I'll work with infra to prepare the 72-hour sample and aim to share a link by Thursday.

Appreciate the clear options — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering | PineCard
alicia@pinecard.io

Great — thanks for the quick replies, Alicia. Two small updates: we can size a phased pilot to stay under $45k (phased capacity + crediting model), and the S3 72-hour anonymized export will be perfect for our TCO assumptions.

Karthik & Marissa: looping you both in to run the ops/plan side. Karthik, can you sketch a minimal Dedicated capacity profile that fits under a $45k pilot (ideally 30 days, burstable at settlement window)? Marissa, can you draft an onboarding checklist for the Private option with the KMS ARN and redaction requirements Alicia mentioned.

Proposed timeline
- Thu (10/14): PineCard shares 72-hour sample + confirm $45k pilot cap.
- Fri (10/15): Redwood delivers TCO workbook + two pilot configs (Scope A minimal, Scope B target).
- Mon (10/18): 15–30 minute alignment call to pick the pilot and agree on dates.

If PineCard confirms $45k, we'll prioritize a Scope A phased plan that demonstrates the batching & KV benefits within the cap.

Attachments (resending): redwood-tco-draft.xlsx

Thanks,
Vanessa

Thanks for the ping — quick ops notes and an initial capacity sketch.

Ops notes
- We can build a phased Dedicated pool: Phase 1 (demo-cap) = 2 GPUs reserved for 30 days + burst to 4 GPUs during 14:00–16:30 PT via pre-warmed queues. Estimated committed cost (infra only) ~ $28k for 30 days; adds networking/KMS + Redwood service layer ~ $10–12k => total ~ $38–40k. That keeps us under the $45k pilot cap assuming some credits.
- Scope A (30d) will show batching delta for settlement flows; Scope B adds KV cache + quantized variant and needs extra validation time.

Immediate asks for TCO accuracy
- Please confirm estimated average tokens per settlement request in sample (the S3 export schema helps).
- Are attachments (receipts) currently stripped before settlement call? If not, point us to where those appear so we can include token delta.

I'll populate the capacity numbers into redwood-tco-draft.xlsx and share updates to the Drive link Vanessa included. Marissa — can you draft the onboarding checklist items (KMS ARN, redaction policy, infra contacts) and I'll attach.

Karthik
